punchline: In one sleep study, people got roughly 20 to 30 percent faster at a typing sequence overnight, without practising it again.
thirty_sec: Matthew Walker's lab taught people a finger sequence with their non-dominant hand. Then some were retested after a night's sleep, others after the same hours awake. Only the sleepers improved, by roughly 20 to 30 percent in speed, and more accurate too. The gain tracked a type of sleep that's packed into the last hours of the night. So when you set an early alarm, you're cutting exactly the part that locks in what you practised.
question: Have you ever practised something that suddenly clicked the next day? How had you slept?
